plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped pink-lilac flowers in autumn with no leaves present. The strap-like leaves appear in spring and die back by summer, which gives it the nickname 'naked ladies'. All parts are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Meadows and woodlands of Europe, widely cultivated in temperate gardens in North America and Asia
plants.funFact: Colchicum is the source of colchicine, a compound used in treating gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, hardy native North American perennial covered in daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It thrives in moist meadows and roadsides and is a critical late-season nectar source for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Quebec to Alabama and west to the Rockies
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies rely heavily on New England asters for fuel during their autumn migration to Mexico.

plants.name: Osmanthus fragrans
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree bearing clusters of tiny, intensely apricot-scented flowers. It is celebrated across East Asia for its fragrance, used in teas, cakes, and perfumes.
plants.location: Native to China, cultivated in Japan, Southeast Asia, and the southern United States
plants.funFact: Guilin in China is named for the osmanthus ('gui'), and its blooming coincides with the Mid-Autumn Festival, when osmanthus cakes and wine are enjoyed.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular deciduous tree that blankets streets and parks in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers before the fern-like leaves fully emerge. In the Southern Hemisphere it blooms in spring.
plants.location: Native to South America, widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Brisbane, Sydney), and Argentina
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed 'Jacaranda City' because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees, and in Australia the blooms were traditionally said to signal university exams.
